ja: ご心配ですよね。お気持ちわかります。
before: You must be worried. I understand.
after: You must be worried. I understand.

ja: まず、安心してください。
before: First, please don't worry.
after: First, please don't worry.

ja: これは子どもによくあることです。
before: This is very common in children.
after: This is very common in children.

ja: 本当の◯◯ではありません。むしろ△△です。
before: It isn't really ___. It's more like ___.
after: It isn't really ___. It's more like ___.

ja: 一番大事なのは、〜です。
before: The main thing is ___.
after: The main thing is ___.

ja: その都度、しっかり治していきましょう。
before: Let's treat it properly each time.
after: Let's treat it properly each time.

ja: 一緒に様子を見ていきましょう。
before: Let's watch how she does. We'll do it together.
after: Let's keep an eye on how she's doing together.

ja: ですから、心配いりません。
before: So, please don't worry.
after: So, please don't worry.

ja: 何かあれば、いつでも来てください。
before: If anything happens, please come back anytime.
after: If anything happens, please come back anytime.

ja: 焦らず、少しずつ良くしていきましょう。
before: No rush. Let's get her better step by step.
after: There's no rush. Let's help her get better, step by step.

ja: 私は小児外科医です。子どものお腹と栄養を診ています。
before: I'm a pediatric surgeon. I take care of children's tummy problems and nutrition.
after: I'm a pediatric surgeon. I look after children with tummy problems and help with their nutrition.

ja: 今日はお子さんの状態を説明して、一緒に方針を決めましょう。
before: Today, I'll explain how she is doing. Then we'll decide the plan together.
after: Today, I'll explain how she's doing. Then we'll make a plan together.

ja: 熱と咳、ゼーゼーが続いて、ご心配ですよね。
before: She has had fever, cough, and wheezing. You must be worried.
after: She's had a fever, a cough, and wheezing. I can understand why you're worried.

ja: まず安心してください。RSウイルスの検査は陰性でした。
before: First, please don't worry. Her RSV test was negative.
after: First, please don't worry. Her RSV test was negative.

ja: 子どもは風邪をひくと、気道が敏感になってゼーゼーします。
before: When children get a cold, their airways get sensitive. So they wheeze.
after: When children get a cold, their airways get sensitive. So they wheeze.

ja: 喘息のようなゼーゼーですが、ほとんどの場合、本当の喘息ではありません。
before: It sounds like asthma. But in most cases, it is not true asthma.
after: It sounds like asthma. But in most cases, it is not true asthma.
context_review: 「本当の喘息ではない」の対象・年齢・診断条件を明示したい。

ja: 酸素の値は問題ありません。ただ、ゼーゼーで夜眠りにくくなります。
before: Her oxygen level is fine. But the wheezing can make it hard to sleep at night.
after: Her oxygen level is fine. But the wheezing can make it hard to sleep at night.

ja: クリニックで吸入をしました。気道を広げて楽にする薬です。
before: We did a nebulizer treatment here. It opens the airways. It makes breathing easier.
after: We gave her a nebulizer treatment here. The medicine opens her airways and helps her breathe more easily.

ja: 長く続く治療は要りません。風邪のたびにしっかり治すことが大事です。
before: She doesn't need long-term treatment. But each time she gets a cold, we treat it well.
after: She doesn't need long-term treatment. But each time she gets a cold, we treat it well.

ja: 今すぐ「喘息」と決めつける必要はありません。
before: We don't need to call this asthma right now.
after: We don't need to call this asthma right now.

ja: 大事なのは診断名より、今の気道の炎症をしっかり取ることです。
before: Right now, treating the inflammation in her airways matters more than the name.
after: Right now, treating the inflammation in her airways matters more than the name.

ja: 炎症をしっかり取ってリセットすると、本人も楽になり、次のゼーゼーの予防にもなります。
before: Once we clear the inflammation, her airways get a reset. She feels better. And it helps prevent the next wheezing.
after: Treating the inflammation gives her airways a chance to recover. It helps her feel better and helps prevent another episode of wheezing.

ja: 目標はシンプルです。夜ぐっすり眠れて、楽に呼吸できること。
before: We want her to sleep well at night and breathe easily.
after: We want her to sleep well at night and breathe easily.

ja: 小さな子は、風邪をひくとすぐにゼーゼーしやすいんです。
before: Small children often wheeze as soon as they get a cold.
after: Small children often wheeze as soon as they get a cold.

ja: この子も、風邪のたびにゼーゼーしていますね。
before: She wheezes every time she catches a cold, doesn't she?
after: She wheezes every time she catches a cold, doesn't she?

ja: ゼーゼーが3回以上あって、気管支を広げる吸入で治まる場合は、いったん「小児喘息」と呼びます。
before: If she wheezes three or more times, and it gets better with a nebulizer treatment, we call it childhood asthma for now.
after: If she wheezes three or more times, and it gets better with a nebulizer treatment, we call it childhood asthma for now.
context_review: 3回以上＋吸入反応だけで診断が完結するように聞こえる。適用条件の確認が必要。

ja: でも、ほとんどは一時的なもので、本当の喘息になる子はごくわずかです。
before: But in most cases, it is temporary. Very few children get true asthma.
after: But in most cases, it is temporary. Very few children get true asthma.
context_review: 「ごくわずか」の対象集団と根拠を確認したい。

ja: その都度、風邪の治療と、敏感になった気道の治療をしっかり行います。
before: Each time, we treat the cold. And we treat the sensitive airways.
after: Each time, we treat her cold and help calm her sensitive airways.

ja: 炎症をしっかり取っていけば、ほとんどの子は大きくなるにつれて治っていきます。
before: If we clear the inflammation each time, most children grow out of it.
after: If we clear the inflammation each time, most children grow out of it.
context_review: 炎症治療と成長による改善の因果関係が強く聞こえる。

ja: ごく一部の子だけが、本当の喘息として長く治療が必要になります。
before: Only a few children have true asthma. They need long-term treatment.
after: Only a few children have true asthma. They need long-term treatment.
context_review: 長期治療が必要な割合を一般化しない。

ja: 今の風邪薬は続けてください。今日、追加でお出しします。
before: Please keep giving the current cold medicine. I'll give you more today.
after: Please keep giving her the cold medicine she's taking now. I'll prescribe some more today.

ja: 熱が数日続いて、中耳炎と軽い気管支炎が出ています。
before: She has had a fever for a few days. Now she has an ear infection and mild bronchitis.
after: She has had a fever for a few days. Now she has an ear infection and mild bronchitis.

ja: なので抗生物質を新しく足します。両方きちんと飲ませてください。
before: So, I'll add an antibiotic. Please give her both medicines.
after: So, I'll add an antibiotic. Please give her both medicines.

ja: まずは熱が下がるか、鼻や胸の症状が良くなるかを見ていきましょう。
before: First, let's see if the fever comes down. And let's see if her nose and chest get better.
after: First, let's see if her fever comes down and her nose and chest symptoms improve.

ja: 熱が下がらなければ、木曜か金曜にまた来てください。
before: If the fever doesn't come down, please come back on Thursday or Friday.
after: If the fever doesn't come down, please come back on Thursday or Friday.

ja: 夜の咳がひどい時は、診療時間内なら予約なしで吸入に来られます。この特急券をどうぞ。
before: If her cough is bad at night, you can come for a nebulizer treatment. No appointment needed, during clinic hours. Here is an express ticket.
after: If her cough is bad at night, you can come for a nebulizer treatment. No appointment needed, during clinic hours. Here is an express ticket.

ja: これだけは救急へ：横になって全く眠れない。
before: Please go to the ER for these signs. She can't sleep at all lying down.
after: Please go to the ER for these signs. She can't sleep at all lying down.

ja: 肩やお腹を使って息をしている。目がうつろ。
before: She is using her shoulders or belly to breathe. Or her eyes look dazed.
after: She is using her shoulders or belly to breathe. Or her eyes look dazed.

ja: 集団生活を始めた子が、毎週のように風邪をひくのは、異常ではありません。
before: A child who just started daycare gets a cold almost every week. This is normal.
after: A child who just started daycare gets a cold almost every week. This is normal.

ja: 今は、体が初めてのウイルスに出会って、免疫を一つずつ学んでいる最中です。
before: Right now, her body is meeting new viruses for the first time. It's building immunity one by one.
after: Her body is meeting these viruses for the first time. It's learning to fight them, one by one.

ja: 3ヶ月から半年ほどで、少しずつ強くなって山を越えます。
before: Over three to six months, she gets stronger little by little. Then it gets easier.
after: Over three to six months, she gets stronger little by little. Then it gets easier.

ja: 完治を狙わなくて大丈夫。つらい症状を楽にしながら、根気よく付き合いましょう。
before: We don't need a perfect cure. Let's ease the hard symptoms. And let's be patient together.
after: We don't have to get rid of every symptom. Let's help her feel more comfortable and take it one step at a time.

ja: 熱が続くときは、元気そうでも3日目あたりに一度受診してください。
before: If the fever continues, please come in around day three. Even if she seems fine.
after: If the fever continues, please come in around day three. Even if she seems fine.

ja: 熱が下がるまでは、一緒に経過を見せてください。風邪以外の原因も見逃さないためです。
before: Until the fever comes down, please keep coming in. That way we don't miss anything other than a cold.
after: Until the fever comes down, please keep coming in. That way we don't miss anything other than a cold.

ja: 解熱して24時間たって元気なら、登園できます。
before: She can go back to daycare once she's been fever-free for 24 hours and feels well.
after: She can go back to daycare once she's been fever-free for 24 hours and feels well.

ja: 咳だけ長く残るのは、気道が敏感になっているからです。つらいときは炎症をしっかり取ります。
before: A cough can stay for a while. That's because her airways are sensitive. If it's hard on her, we treat the inflammation.
after: A cough can stay for a while. That's because her airways are sensitive. If it's hard on her, we treat the inflammation.

ja: どうか、ご自分を責めないでください。お父さん・お母さんの体調も大切にしてください。
before: Please don't blame yourself. And please take care of your own health too.
after: Please don't blame yourself. And please take care of your own health too.

ja: 何度風邪をひいても大丈夫。少しずつ、強くなっていきます。
before: It's okay if she gets many colds. Little by little, she is getting stronger.
after: It's okay if she gets many colds. Little by little, she is getting stronger.

ja: 胃腸炎で一番こわいのは脱水です。
before: With a stomach bug, the biggest worry is dehydration.
after: With a stomach bug, the biggest worry is dehydration.

ja: 吐き気が強い間（半日ほど）は、無理に飲ませないでください。
before: While the nausea is strong, for about half a day, don't force her to drink.
after: While the nausea is strong, for about half a day, don't force her to drink.
context_review: 「半日」は飲水中断と誤解され得る。少量頻回の経口補水との整合を院長確認。

ja: 落ち着いてきたら、スプーン一杯を5〜15分おきに、点滴みたいに少しずつ。
before: When it settles, give one spoonful every 5 to 15 minutes. Slowly, like a drip.
after: When it settles, give one spoonful every 5 to 15 minutes. Slowly, like a drip.

ja: 一気に飲ませると、また吐きやすいので、少しずつ。
before: If she drinks a lot at once, she will throw up again. So, little by little.
after: If she drinks a lot at once, she may throw up again. So give her a little at a time.

ja: 水分が取れたら、お粥やうどんなど消化のいいものから。
before: When she can keep fluids down, start with easy foods. Rice porridge or noodles are good.
after: Once she can keep fluids down, start with foods that are easy to digest, like rice porridge or noodles.

ja: 下痢の間は、牛乳や乳製品は控えめに。
before: Give less milk and dairy while she has diarrhea.
after: Give less milk and dairy while she has diarrhea.
context_review: 乳製品を控える対象条件を確認。NICEは通常のミルク再開を含めて推奨。

ja: 数日食べられなくても、水分と塩分・糖分が取れていれば大丈夫です。
before: Even if she can't eat for a few days, that's okay. She just needs fluids, salt, and sugar.
after: Even if she can't eat for a few days, that's okay. She just needs fluids, salt, and sugar.
context_review: 数日食べられない場合の安全性は脱水・全身状態などに依存する。

ja: 下痢でお尻がかぶれます。赤くなる前にワセリンで守りましょう。
before: Diarrhea can make her bottom sore. Put Vaseline on it before it turns red.
after: Diarrhea can make her bottom sore. Put Vaseline on it before it turns red.

ja: もし吐いても、焦らなくて大丈夫。少し戻して、また少しずつで大丈夫です。
before: If she throws up, don't worry. Take a short break. Then start again, little by little.
after: If she throws up, don't worry. Take a short break. Then start again, little by little.

ja: ぐったり、目がうつろ、8〜10時間おしっこが出ない——これは夜でも救急へ。
before: If she is very limp, her eyes look empty, or no pee for 8 to 10 hours, go to the ER. Even at night.
after: If she is very limp, her eyes look empty, or no pee for 8 to 10 hours, go to the ER. Even at night.

ja: 便が硬いこと＝便秘、とは限りません。大事なのは、すっきり出し切れているかです。
before: Hard stool does not always mean constipation. The important thing is, can she empty out completely?
after: Hard stools don't always mean constipation. What matters is whether she can empty her bowels fully.

ja: まず、直腸にたまったうんちを、しっかり出し切ることから始めます。
before: First, we empty the stool that has built up in the rectum.
after: First, let's clear out the stool that's built up in her rectum.

ja: 直腸を出し切るために、浣腸を主役に使います。
before: To empty the rectum, an enema is our main tool.
after: To empty the rectum, an enema is our main tool.

ja: 浣腸は癖になりません。安心してください。
before: Enemas are not habit-forming. Please don't worry.
after: Enemas are not habit-forming. Please don't worry.

ja: 浣腸は、その日のうんちを出すためだけのものではありません。
before: An enema is not just for passing today's stool.
after: An enema is not just for passing today's stool.

ja: 毎日しっかり出すことで、腸のセンサーと押し出す力を取り戻します。
before: By emptying every day, her bowel gets back its sensation and its pushing power.
after: Emptying her bowels every day helps her regain the feeling that she needs to go, and the strength to push the stool out.

ja: お薬を減らせたら治った、ではありません。毎日すっきり出せる習慣が本当のゴールです。
before: Less medicine does not mean she is cured. The real goal is emptying comfortably every day.
after: Less medicine does not mean she is cured. The real goal is emptying comfortably every day.

ja: これは長期戦です。焦らず、少しずつ進めましょう。
before: This takes a long time. No rush. Let's go step by step.
after: This takes a long time. No rush. Let's go step by step.

ja: 硬い便で切れると、痛くて我慢して、もっと便秘になります。その悪循環を断ちます。
before: Hard stool can cause a tear. It hurts, so she holds it in. Then it gets worse. We break that cycle.
after: Hard stools can cause a small tear. Because it hurts, she holds her stool in, which makes the constipation worse. Let's break that cycle.

ja: 今、お子さんがどのステップにいるかを見ながら進めます。
before: We check which step she is at now. Then we move forward.
after: We'll check where she is in her treatment and decide the next step together.

ja: 高い熱だけで、脳がダメになることはありません。
before: A high fever alone won't damage her brain.
after: A high fever alone won't damage her brain.

ja: 熱は、体が病原体と戦っている証拠です。
before: The fever is a sign that her body is fighting the infection.
after: The fever is a sign that her body is fighting the infection.

ja: 解熱剤は病気を治す薬ではなく、つらさを和らげるものです。
before: Fever medicine doesn't cure the illness. It just makes her more comfortable.
after: Fever medicine doesn't cure the illness. It just makes her more comfortable.

ja: 何度で使うかより、「つらそうかどうか」で決めてください。
before: Don't go by the number. Go by how she looks.
after: Decide by how uncomfortable she seems, not just the temperature.

ja: 水分が取れないくらいつらい時、眠れない時に使ってください。
before: Use it when she is too uncomfortable to drink. Or when she can't sleep.
after: Give it if she's too uncomfortable to drink or sleep.

ja: 高熱でも元気そうなら、使わなくて大丈夫です。
before: If she has a high fever but seems fine, you don't need to give it.
after: If she has a high fever but seems fine, you don't need to give it.

ja: 解熱剤は6時間以上あけて、1日3回までです。
before: Give the fever medicine at least six hours apart, up to three times a day.
after: Give the fever medicine at least six hours apart, up to three times a day.
context_review: 薬剤名・処方量がない。投与間隔や回数は薬ごとに確認する。

ja: 坐薬と飲み薬、効き目は同じです。吐く子は坐薬でどうぞ。
before: The suppository and the oral medicine work the same. If she vomits, use the suppository.
after: The suppository and the oral medicine work the same. If she vomits, use the suppository.

ja: 生後3ヶ月未満で38度以上の熱は、夜でもすぐ受診してください。
before: A baby under three months with a fever of 38°C or higher must see a doctor right away. Even at night.
after: A baby under three months with a fever of 38°C or higher must see a doctor right away. Even at night.

ja: 数字に振り回されず、お子さんの様子を見てあげてください。
before: Don't worry too much about the number. Look at how she is doing.
after: Don't worry too much about the number. Look at how she is doing.

ja: けいれんが起きても、まず落ち着いて。大丈夫です。
before: If she has a seizure, first stay calm. It will be okay.
after: If she has a seizure, first stay calm. It will be okay.
context_review: 「大丈夫」の保証が強い。救急受診条件の説明と一緒に用いる。

ja: 多くは数分で止まります。安全な場所で横向きに寝かせて、見守ってあげてください。
before: Most seizures stop in a few minutes. Lay her on her side in a safe place. Then just watch her.
after: Most seizures stop in a few minutes. Lay her on her side in a safe place. Then just watch her.

ja: 吐いたら、窒息しないよう、体ごと顔を横向きに。
before: If she vomits, turn her whole body to the side. So she doesn't choke.
after: If she vomits, turn her whole body onto her side so she doesn't choke.

ja: 口に何かを入れたり、押さえつけたりは絶対にしないでください。
before: Never put anything in her mouth, and don't hold her down.
after: Never put anything in her mouth, and don't hold her down.

ja: 5分以上止まらないときは、救急車を呼んでください。
before: If it doesn't stop in five minutes, call an ambulance.
after: If it doesn't stop in five minutes, call an ambulance.

ja: 初めてのけいれんや、怖いと思ったら、迷わず救急車で大丈夫です。
before: If it's her first seizure, or you feel scared, just call an ambulance. That's fine.
after: If it's her first seizure, or you feel scared, just call an ambulance. That's fine.

ja: けいれんが止まっても、意識が戻らない・反応が鈍いときは、救急車を呼んでください。
before: After it stops, if she doesn't wake up, or doesn't respond well, call an ambulance.
after: After it stops, if she doesn't wake up, or doesn't respond well, call an ambulance.

ja: 可能なら、けいれんの長さと様子を覚えておいてください。
before: If you can, remember how long it lasted and what it looked like.
after: If you can, remember how long it lasted and what it looked like.

ja: （子へ）これから、お体を診させてね。
before: Let me take a look at you, okay?
after: Let me take a look at you, okay?

ja: （子へ）もしもし、させてね。ちょっと冷たいよ。
before: Let me listen to your chest. It might feel a little cold.
after: Let me listen to your chest. It might feel a little cold.

ja: （子へ）大きく息を吸って。はい、吐いて。
before: Take a big breath in. And out.
after: Take a big breath in. And out.

ja: （子へ）お口を開けて、あーん。
before: Open wide and say 'ahh.'
after: Open wide and say 'ahh.'

ja: （子へ）お喉を見せてね。上手だね！
before: Let me see your throat. Good job!
after: Let me see your throat. Good job!

ja: （子へ）今度はお耳を見るね。じっとしててね。
before: Now let me look in your ears. Hold still.
after: Now I'll look in your ears. Can you stay still for me?

ja: （子へ）はい、おしまい！よく頑張ったね。
before: All done! You did great.
after: All done! You did great.

ja: （親へ）肺の音はきれいです。問題ありません。
before: Her lungs sound clear. No problem there.
after: Her lungs sound clear. No problem there.

ja: （親へ）耳も見ましたが、中耳炎はありません。
before: I checked her ears too. There is no ear infection.
after: I checked her ears too. There is no ear infection.

ja: （親へ）診断は、いわゆる風邪です。
before: The diagnosis is a common cold.
after: She has a common cold.

ja: （親へ）風邪のお薬を出しておきますね。
before: I'll give you some cold medicine.
after: I'll give you some cold medicine.

ja: （親へ）心配はいりませんよ。
before: Please don't worry.
after: Please don't worry.

ja: （親へ）保育園も、行って大丈夫です。
before: And she can go to daycare.
after: And she can go to daycare.

ja: （子へ）今から、お鼻の検査をするね。
before: Now I'm going to do a quick test in your nose, okay?
after: Now I'm going to do a quick test in your nose, okay?

ja: （子へ）お口で、ゆっくり息をしてね。
before: Breathe slowly through your mouth.
after: Breathe slowly through your mouth.

ja: （子へ）力を抜いて、リラックスしてね。
before: Just relax your body.
after: Try to relax for me.

ja: （子へ）細い綿棒が、ゆっくり入るよ。
before: A thin swab is going in slowly.
after: I'll gently put this thin swab into your nose.

ja: （子へ）頭を動かさないでね。
before: Keep your head still for me.
after: Keep your head still for me.

ja: （子へ）ちょっとムズムズするけど、すぐ終わるよ。
before: It might tickle a little, but it'll be over soon.
after: It might tickle a little, but it'll be over soon.

ja: （子へ）はい、おしまい！よく頑張ったね。
before: All done! You were so brave.

ja: おうちを、安心して出せる場所にするのが一番大事です。学校はそのあとで大丈夫です。
before: First, make home a safe place to poop. School can come later.
after: First, make home a safe place to poop. School can come later.

ja: 毎日、家で必ず出せる時間を作りましょう。
before: Let's make a time every day when she can poop at home.
after: Let's set aside time every day for her to use the toilet at home.

ja: 赤ちゃんは、いきむのがまだ下手なだけです。病気ではありません。
before: Babies just aren't good at pushing yet. It's not an illness.
after: Babies just aren't good at pushing yet. It's not an illness.
context_review: 乳児の排便困難すべてに使わず、診断した状態に合わせる。

ja: 綿棒でお尻をやさしく刺激して、出す練習をしてあげましょう。
before: Gently stimulate her bottom with a cotton swab. That helps her practice.
after: Gently stimulate her bottom with a cotton swab. That helps her practice.
context_review: 綿棒刺激の適応と方法を伴う説明が必要。

ja: 大きくなるにつれて、上手になっていきます。
before: She'll get better at it as she grows.
after: She'll get better at it as she grows.

ja: 病気ではないけれど、本来の力が出せない。もどかしいですよね。
before: It's not an illness. But she can't do her best. That must be frustrating.
after: She's not ill, but she isn't feeling her best. I can understand how frustrating that is.

ja: 根性や気持ちの問題ではなく、体の仕組みによるものです。
before: It's not about willpower. It's about how the body works.
after: It's not about willpower. It's about how the body works.

ja: 細胞がエネルギーを作る「バッテリー」が足りていないのかもしれません。
before: Her cells may not have enough battery to make energy.
after: Her cells may not have what they need to make energy. It's a bit like running low on battery power.

ja: 血糖値が急に上がって一気に下がる、ジェットコースターのような動きです。
before: Her blood sugar goes up fast and drops fast. Like a roller coaster.
after: Her blood sugar rises quickly and then drops sharply, like a roller coaster.

ja: 薬は「流す・動かす」はできても、体を「作る」ことはできません。
before: Medicine can move things along. But it can't build the body.
after: Medicine can move things along. But it can't build the body.

ja: 病気がないかも確かめますが、主に栄養の状態を詳しく見ます。
before: We'll check for illness too. But mainly, we'll look closely at her nutrition.
after: We'll check for illness too. But mainly, we'll look closely at her nutrition.

ja: 「基準範囲内」は、「ちょうど良い」という意味ではありません。
before: Within the normal range does not mean just right.
after: Being within the normal range doesn't always mean it's the right level for her.

ja: 一番大事なのは、フェリチン（体に貯めてある鉄）です。
before: The most important number is ferritin. That's the iron stored in the body.
after: The most important number is ferritin. That's the iron stored in the body.
context_review: フェリチンが最重要となる対象を確認。栄養評価全般の断定にしない。

ja: 貧血の値が下がるのは、鉄不足の一番最後です。だからフェリチンを見ます。
before: Hemoglobin drops last when iron is low. That's why we look at ferritin.
after: Hemoglobin drops last when iron is low. That's why we look at ferritin.
context_review: フェリチン・ヘモグロビンの解釈には病態の文脈が必要。

ja: （例）17から35へ、倍くらいになりました。
before: It went from 17 to 35. About double.
after: It went from 17 to 35. About double.

ja: まずは、悩みが取れるところまで上げるのが第一ステップです。
before: The first step is to raise it until her symptoms get better.
after: The first step is to raise it until her symptoms get better.
context_review: 症状が改善するまで数値を上げる、という目標設定の条件を確認。

ja: フェリチンとタンパク質、この2つで8割は分かります。
before: Ferritin and protein. These two tell us about 80 percent.
after: Ferritin and protein. These two tell us about 80 percent.
context_review: 「8割」は何の8割か、根拠と対象の確認が必要。

ja: 減らすのではなく、タンパク質を足していきましょう。
before: Don't cut things out. Let's add protein.
after: Don't cut things out. Let's add protein.

ja: 朝ごはんに、卵やチーズを一品足すだけでも違います。
before: Just adding an egg or some cheese to breakfast makes a difference.
after: Just adding an egg or some cheese to breakfast makes a difference.

ja: 毎食、その子の両手のひらに乗るくらいのタンパク質が目安です。
before: At every meal, aim for protein about the size of her two palms.
after: At each meal, aim for a portion of protein-rich food about the size of her two palms.
context_review: 両手のひらサイズはたんぱく質そのものの重量ではなく食品の量。年齢・対象を確認。

ja: 甘いものは、完全に禁止しなくていいです。食べたあとに少し体を動かしましょう。
before: You don't have to ban sweets. Just have her move a little after eating them.
after: You don't have to ban sweets. Just have her move a little after eating them.

ja: サプリは、自分の食事で足りるようになるまでの、一時的な補助輪です。
before: Supplements are temporary training wheels. Until she gets enough from food.
after: Supplements are like training wheels. They're temporary support until she can get enough from food.

ja: 鉄を飲むと便が黒っぽくなることがありますが、心配いりません。
before: Iron can make her stool dark. That's normal. Don't worry.
after: Iron can make her stool dark. That's normal. Don't worry.

ja: 良くなったらやめて大丈夫です。要らなくなることが目標です。
before: When she's better, she can stop. The goal is not to need them.
after: When she's better, she can stop. The goal is not to need them.
context_review: 中止する対象サプリと判断者を明示したい。

ja: 2〜3週間後に結果が出たら、一緒に方針を決めましょう。
before: The results come in two to three weeks. Then let's decide the plan together.
after: When the results come back in two or three weeks, we'll make a plan together.

ja: 3か月後に、もう一度採血しましょう。
before: Let's recheck her blood in three months.
after: Let's recheck her blood in three months.

ja: 3か月から半年で、「変わってきた」と感じられるのが目標です。
before: The goal is that you notice a change in three to six months.
after: Our goal is for you to notice a change in three to six months.

ja: いつから始めても、遅すぎることはありません。
before: It's never too late to start.
after: It's never too late to start.

ja: 完璧を目指さず、できそうなことを一つ試してみましょう。
before: Don't aim for perfect. Let's try one thing you can do.
after: It doesn't have to be perfect. Let's try one thing that feels manageable.

ja: 夜中に血糖が下がって、朝起きる力が出ないのかもしれません。
before: Her blood sugar may drop during the night. So she has no energy in the morning.
after: Her blood sugar may be dropping during the night. That could be why she has so little energy in the morning.
context_review: 夜間低血糖は未確認の可能性として保った。診断された事実には変えない。

ja: 寝る前のジュースやゼリーは、やめてみましょう。
before: Let's stop juice and jelly before bed.
after: Let's try avoiding juice and jelly before bed.

ja: 寝る前は、甘いものの代わりに豆乳などにしてみましょう。
before: Before bed, try soy milk instead of something sweet.
after: Before bed, try soy milk instead of something sweet.

ja: 最初は、保険の採血からで大丈夫です。
before: We can start with a basic blood test. It's covered by insurance.
after: We can start with a basic blood test. It's covered by insurance.

ja: 頭痛も、鉄が足りないことと関係していることがあります。
before: Headaches can also be linked to low iron.
after: Headaches can also be linked to low iron.

ja: 熱性けいれんの多くは数分で止まり、後に何も残りません。
before: Most febrile seizures stop in a few minutes. They don't leave any damage.
after: Most febrile seizures stop in a few minutes. They don't leave any damage.

ja: 次に熱が出たときの目安を、お伝えしておきますね。
before: Let me tell you what to watch for the next time she has a fever.
after: Let me tell you what to watch for the next time she has a fever.

ja: 子どもの頃から、手先が器用でした。
before: As a child, I was good with my hands.
after: As a child, I was good with my hands.

ja: 機械いじりが好きで、何かを作るのが好きでした。
before: I loved taking machines apart. I loved making things.
after: I loved tinkering with machines and making things.

ja: 医学部のとき、小児外科に「作る未来」を感じました。
before: In medical school, I felt pediatric surgery had a creative future.
after: In medical school, I saw pediatric surgery as a way to help build a child's future.

ja: だから小児外科に進みました。
before: So I chose pediatric surgery.
after: So I chose pediatric surgery.

ja: 手術という技術で、小さな赤ちゃんの命を助ける仕事です。
before: We use surgery to save the lives of tiny babies.
after: We use surgery to save the lives of tiny babies.

ja: でも、長くやっているうちに、悩みが出てきました。
before: But over the years, something started to bother me.
after: But over the years, something started to bother me.

ja: 手術で診る病気は、いわば「なれの果て」です。
before: The diseases we operate on are the end of a long road.
after: The diseases we operate on are the end of a long road.

ja: もっと手前で、できることがあるのではないか。
before: I thought, there must be something we can do earlier.
after: I began to wonder if there was more we could do before children got to that point.

ja: 地域の中で子どもを診るうちに、その目線が育ちました。
before: As I worked with children in the community, I began to see things that way.
after: As I worked with children in the community, I began to see things that way.

ja: その答えが、栄養でした。
before: The answer was nutrition.
after: The answer was nutrition.

ja: 細胞も、元気も、栄養から作られます。
before: Our cells are made from nutrition. So is our energy.
after: The food we eat provides what our bodies need to build cells and make energy.

ja: 病気の治りやすさも、風邪のひきにくさも、心の健康も、栄養と関係しています。
before: How fast we recover, how often we catch colds, even our mood. Nutrition is behind all of them.
after: Nutrition is linked to how well we recover, how often we catch colds, and our mental health.

ja: 「病気ではないけれど元気がない」子の多くが、栄養の視点で説明できるようになりました。
before: Many children are not sick, but not well either. Nutrition explains a lot of that.
after: Looking at nutrition helped me understand many children who weren't ill but still didn't feel well.

ja: 今は、この学問に魅了されて、夢中です。
before: Now I'm fascinated by this field. I'm hooked.
after: Now I'm fascinated by this field. I'm hooked.

ja: 現場で手応えを感じています。
before: And I can see it working in my clinic.
after: And I can see it working in my clinic.

ja: これを日本中に広めていきたいと思っています。
before: I want to spread this across Japan.
after: I'd like to share this approach with people across Japan.

ja: 一番大事なのは、何が本質で、本当で、本物なのかです。
before: What matters most to me is what is real, true, and genuine.
after: What matters most to me is what is real, true, and genuine.

ja: 原則に沿って生きること。感謝すること。
before: Living by principles. Being grateful.
after: I try to live by my principles and remember to be grateful.

ja: 助け合い、分かち合うこと。
before: Helping each other. Sharing.
after: I believe in helping each other and sharing what we have.

ja: そして、成長や感動の喜びを世界に伝えること。それが私のミッションです。
before: And sharing the joy of growing and being moved. That's my mission.
after: My mission is to share the joy of growth and the experiences that move us, with people around the world.

ja: 人生のほとんどを、医療の中で過ごしてきました。
before: I've spent most of my life in medicine.
after: I've spent most of my life in medicine.

ja: その視点を広げて、もっと多くの人の心と体を支えたいです。
before: I want to use that to support more people, in body and mind.
after: I'd like to broaden my perspective and help more people care for both their body and mind.

ja: 正直に言うと、これまで働きすぎました。
before: To be honest, I've worked too much.
after: To be honest, I've worked too much.

ja: だから今は、いろいろな場所に行って、刺激を受けることも大事にしています。
before: So now, I also want to travel more, and see new things.
after: So now I also make time to travel, see new places, and find inspiration.

ja: 今回のスペイン旅行も、その一つです。
before: This trip to Spain is part of that.
after: This trip to Spain is part of that.

ja: 不器用でもいい。要領が悪くてもいい。
before: It's okay to be clumsy. It's okay to be slow.
after: It's okay if things don't come easily. It's okay to take the long way round.

ja: でも、正直に、誠実に生きることが大事です。
before: But be honest. Live with integrity. That's what matters.
after: What matters to me is living honestly and treating people with sincerity.

ja: そして、本物を見分ける目を持つこと。
before: And know what is real when you see it.
after: And I want to be able to recognize what's real and worthwhile.

ja: 私が一番大事にしているのは、そこです。
before: That's what I care about most.
after: That's what I care about most.

ja: 正直に言うと、
before: To be honest,
after: To be honest,

ja: あれが転機でした。
before: That was the turning point for me.
after: That was the turning point for me.

ja: 一番うれしいのは、〜のときです。
before: The happiest moment for me is when ___.
after: The happiest moment for me is when ___.

ja: あの瞬間、心を動かされました。
before: That moment really moved me.
after: That moment really moved me.

ja: うまく言えないのですが、
before: It's hard to put into words, but
after: It's hard to put into words, but

ja: それが、この仕事を続ける理由です。
before: That's why I keep doing this work.
after: That's why I keep doing this work.

ja: お腹と栄養の、子ども専門のクリニックです。
before: My clinic is for children. We focus on gut health and nutrition.
after: My clinic is for children. We focus on gut health and nutrition.

ja: 便秘の子どもを、年間5,000組ほど診ています。
before: I see about 5,000 children a year for constipation.
after: I see about 5,000 children and their families a year for constipation.
context_review: 5,000組が実人数・延べ受診数のどちらかは今回確認していない。

ja: 手術台で、病気の一番下流を見てきました。だから、上流に持ち場を移しました。
before: As a surgeon, I treated children who needed surgery. Now I focus on helping children earlier. That's what I mean by moving upstream.
after: As a surgeon, I treated children who needed surgery. Now I focus on helping children earlier. That's what I mean by moving upstream.

ja: メスを置いて、スプーンを持ちました。
before: I put down the scalpel and picked up a spoon.
after: I put down the scalpel and picked up a spoon.

ja: 腕はそのままに、持ち場を上流に移した外科医です。
before: I'm still a surgeon. I just moved my work upstream.
after: I'm still a surgeon. I just moved my work upstream.

ja: 栄養は、心と体の土台です。
before: Nutrition is the foundation of the body and the mind.
after: Nutrition is the foundation of the body and the mind.

ja: 焦らず、今のペースで大丈夫です。
before: No rush. Your pace is fine.
after: There's no rush. We can go at your pace.

ja: 引き続き、一緒に見ていきましょう。
before: Let's keep watching her together.
after: Let's keep following her progress together.

ja: ゴールは、医療に頼らなくていい状態＝卒業です。
before: The goal is to graduate. To not need us anymore.
after: The goal is for her to graduate from our care, so she no longer needs medical support.

ja: 農場と同じです。今日タネをまいても、明日には実りません。
before: It's like a farm. You plant a seed today. It doesn't grow by tomorrow.
after: It's like farming. You can't plant seeds today and expect a harvest tomorrow.

ja: 一進一退でいいんです。根気よく続けることが大事です。
before: Two steps forward, one step back is fine. Just keep going.
after: Two steps forward, one step back is fine. Just keep going.

ja: 今の食事を否定しません。土台に足し算していきましょう。
before: I'm not saying her current diet is wrong. Let's build on it.
after: I'm not saying her current diet is wrong. Let's build on it.

ja: お薬はメガネと同じです。見えるようになるための道具です。
before: Medicine is like glasses. It's a tool that helps her function.
after: Medicine is like glasses. It's a tool that helps her function.

ja: 病気ではなく体質です。意志や根性の問題ではありません。
before: It's not an illness. It's how her body works. It's not about willpower.
after: It's not an illness. It's how her body works. It's not about willpower.

ja: ご自分を責めないでください。治療で良くなっていきます。
before: Please don't blame yourself. With treatment, she will get better.
after: Please don't blame yourself. With treatment, she will get better.

ja: 大事なのは、本人が困っているかどうかです。
before: What matters is whether she is struggling.
after: What matters is whether she is struggling.

ja: 本当の健康を土台に、一人ひとりが自分らしく人生を楽しめるように。
before: Real health is the base. Then each person can enjoy life in their own way.
after: Good health is the foundation. I want each person to enjoy life in their own way.

ja: 本来持っている生命力を取り戻すことを支える。それが中心軸です。
before: I help children get back the strength they were born with. That's what matters most to me.
after: I help children get back the strength they were born with. That's what matters most to me.

ja: 座右の銘は「天を相手に仕事をする」です。
before: My motto is: work as if heaven is watching, not people.
after: My motto is: work as if heaven is watching, not people.

ja: 人の心に、灯りをともしたい。
before: I want to light a small lamp in people's hearts.
after: I want to light a small lamp in people's hearts.

ja: 可能性は見捨てない。信頼は行動で見る。
before: I never give up on someone's potential. And I judge trust by actions.
after: I don't give up on people's potential. But I look at what they do to decide whether I can trust them.

ja: まず、みんなが喜ぶ世界がある。そこから始めます。
before: First, imagine a world where everyone is happy. I start from there.
after: First, imagine a world where everyone is happy. I start from there.

ja: 原則には厳しく、人にはやさしく。
before: Strict with principles. Kind to people.
after: I hold firmly to my principles, but I try to treat people with kindness.

ja: 作品で導く。生き方は強いない。
before: I lead by what I make. I don't tell people how to live.
after: I try to lead through my work. I don't force my way of life on others.

ja: 静かでいい。短い言葉に、思想と熱を乗せる。
before: Quiet is fine. I put my ideas and my passion into a few words.
after: Quiet is fine. I put my ideas and my passion into a few words.

ja: 私は、楽をしたい人ではありません。挑みたい人です。
before: I'm not looking for an easy life. I want a challenge.
after: I'm not looking for an easy life. I want a challenge.

ja: 使命は突然湧くものではなく、ご縁と経験の中で見つかるものです。
before: A mission doesn't just appear. You find it through people and experience.
after: You don't find your purpose overnight. You find it through the people you meet and the things you experience.

ja: 1ミリでも成長があれば、それでいい。
before: Even one millimeter of growth is enough.
after: Even a millimeter of growth matters to me.

ja: はじめまして。
before: Nice to meet you.
after: Nice to meet you.

ja: （別れ際に）お会いできてよかったです。
before: It was nice meeting you.
after: It was nice meeting you.

after: How are you doing?
